metzcathedral.name: Metz Cathedral
metzcathedral.slogan: The Good Lord's lantern, lit by Chagall.
metzcathedral.line: About 6,500 m² of stained glass, Chagall's included, earned it the nickname 'the Good Lord's Lantern'.

pompidoumetz.name: Centre Pompidou-Metz
pompidoumetz.slogan: A woven wooden hat landed beside the station.
pompidoumetz.line: Shigeru Ban based the roof on a Chinese hat he found in Paris; it covers about 8,000 square metres.

douaumontossuary.name: Douaumont Ossuary
douaumontossuary.slogan: A long hall of silence above the Verdun hills.
douaumontossuary.line: It holds the remains of at least 130,000 unidentified soldiers, French and German, seen through small windows.

portedesallemands.name: Porte des Allemands
portedesallemands.slogan: Round towers and a bridge over the Seille.
portedesallemands.line: Two 13th-century round towers and two 15th-century gun bastions survive from Metz's medieval walls.

hackenbergfort.name: Fort de Hackenberg
hackenbergfort.slogan: An underground town of the Maginot Line, crossed by electric train.
hackenbergfort.line: Hackenberg is the largest fort of the Maginot Line, with about 10 km of tunnels under the hill.
